clue.text: Hazel's dependants have Shakespearean stories read out

indicators.note: read out means the words are spoken, so we want something that sounds like the stories

parts.note: Tales from Shakespeare was written by Charles and Mary Lamb, so Lamb's tales

explanation.surface: Someone called Hazel has children who listen to Shakespeare stories being read aloud to them.
explanation.walkthrough: Hazel looks like a woman's name, but it is the tree: its catkins hang from it. Lamb's Tales from Shakespeare is a classic children's retelling of the plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Catkins of the hazel tree are popularly called lambs' tails, and they hang down from the branches as if dependent on them.

clue.text: Teach girl appearing unusually dull

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of the two words come out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A teacher's pupil is unexpectedly listless in class.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargic means sluggish and lacking energy, which is a sense of dull.

clue.text: Sculptor receives one penny in old money

indicators.note: receives means the sculptor takes the other letters into himself

parts.note: Henry Moore was a famous English sculptor
one is the Roman numeral I
D is the abbreviation for a penny in old British money

explanation.surface: An artist is paid a single penny in pre-decimal coinage.
explanation.definitionFit: A moidore was an old Portuguese gold coin also current in England, so a piece of old money.

clue.text: Support holding up targets that is used in laboratory

indicators.note: holding means the support wraps around the other piece

parts.note: a tee is the peg that supports a golf ball

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word targets is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: butts are archery targets

explanation.surface: A stand holds up practice targets of some sort in a science lab.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reads the archery targets bottom to top; 'Support' is a golf peg, not a lab stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass tube closed at one end, the familiar piece of chemistry apparatus.

clue.text: Barely ten got healthier after treatment

indicators.note: after treatment means the letters are worked over and come out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A ten-year-old patient was less clothed but healthier once treated.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means naked, which matches barely in the sense of without clothes.

clue.text: Singer wanting to bust into a certain opera

indicators.note: bust into means one piece breaks into the middle of another

parts.note: a certain amount is some

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the word to is removed

parts.note: an alto is a singer of the low female or high male voice part
taken as written, the letters to be removed

explanation.surface: A vocalist hopes to burst in on a particular operatic performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' strips the word 'to' from the singer, and 'bust into' breaks the remainder into 'a certain'; 'Singer' is not a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Strauss's one-act opera about the daughter of Herodias, the title used here as an example.

clue.text: This draws attention, and gives you an edge

parts.note: an is the indefinite article A
a hem is the edge of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: Something that attracts notice also gives you an advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an edge' looks like a competitive advantage, but it is A plus HEM.
explanation.definitionFit: The little throat-clearing cough is used to catch someone's notice.

clue.text: Mishaps I'd mishandled in position on board

indicators.note: mishandled means the letters are handled badly and scrambled

explanation.surface: Accidents I mishandled while placed on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Midway along a ship's length is a location aboard the vessel, on board meaning on a ship.

clue.text: Bird overcomes former rival

indicators.note: in a down clue, overcomes means the bird is placed over, above, the other piece

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird
late can mean former, as in the late chairman

explanation.surface: A bird gets the better of an ex-competitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rival' looks like a noun after 'former', but it is a verb: to rival is to match.
explanation.definitionFit: To emulate someone is to try to equal or surpass them, which is to rival them.

clue.text: Dense yokel, entering exam, rejected

indicators.note: entering means the yokel goes into the other piece
rejected means the word for exam is turned back to front

parts.note: a test is an exam
a hick is an unsophisticated country person

explanation.surface: A stupid country bumpkin sits an exam and fails it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dense' looks like a description of the yokel, but it means closely packed; 'rejected' turns the exam back to front before the yokel enters.
explanation.definitionFit: Thickset means solidly built or closely set, as a dense hedge is thickset.

clue.text: Saved from being bedridden?

definitions.meaning: put away or stored for later use

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both stored away for the future and confined to bed with illness.

clue.text: Soon priest's caught out

indicators.note: out means the letter for caught is left out

parts.note: a canon is a member of the clergy
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A cleric is soon to be found out.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old word for shortly or in a little while.

clue.text: This affects hot matters

indicators.note: affects means the letters are acted upon and rearranged

explanation.surface: A device that controls heat influences hot things.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The device regulates temperature, so it affects how hot things become.

clue.text: Dan going openly round town

parts.note: a dan is a grade in judo marked by a coloured belt; here the coloured strip goes round a town as open countryside

explanation.surface: A judo expert parades around town.
explanation.walkthrough: Dan is a judo grade; in Britain a protected ring of open countryside around a town is named for a judo belt colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring of undeveloped open land kept around a town, punning on a judo grade.

clue.text: Shift out of and in prison, with long inside

parts.note: ex means out of, as in ex cathedra

indicators.note: inside means the word for long goes within the word for imprisoned

parts.note: pent means shut up, as in pent up
to long for something is to be dying for it, so die

explanation.surface: Someone moves out and back into jail, with a long stretch inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A shift is a makeshift means of getting by, which is what an expedient is.

clue.text: What one is entitled to say in church services

indicators.note: say means the word is spoken, so we want a soundalike

parts.note: what one is entitled to are one's rights

explanation.surface: What a person may claim to say in church.
explanation.definitionFit: Rites are ceremonies, such as the services held in a church.

clue.text: New design for women's bra and belt

indicators.note: a new design for something rearranges it, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A fresh design for a woman's bra and belt.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sam Browne is a military officer's belt with a strap over the shoulder.

clue.text: Stop and think, with a lot of effort

parts.note: to hold a view is to think it
hard means with great effort, as in working hard

explanation.surface: Pause and consider carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is an exclamation meaning wait or stop, used to halt someone.

clue.text: Men's overalls

definitions.meaning: leather leggings worn over trousers by cowboys

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both fellows and the leather leggings cowboys wear over their trousers.

clue.text: Robin looked upon Marian at first as tough

parts.note: Robin Hood, the outlaw of English legend

indicators.note: at first means take the first letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: Robin gazed at Marian at first, as a hard man.
explanation.walkthrough: Maid Marian is Robin Hood's sweetheart in the legend, which supports the surface. Here 'tough' is a noun, a thug.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough is a rough violent man, a thug, which is what a hoodlum is.

clue.text: Large theatre company with deficit approaches European Union, getting millions

parts.note: a deficit is a loss

explanation.surface: A big theatre company running at a loss turns to the EU and gets millions.
explanation.definitionFit: The Colosseum in Rome is a huge amphitheatre, and the name is used for large theatres.

clue.text: Just a selection from presenter edited and recorded

indicators.note: just a selection from means the letters are a stretch picked out of the two words

explanation.surface: Only part of what a broadcaster edited was put on record.
explanation.definitionFit: Entered means written down in a record or ledger.

clue.text: Lock up after a protest

indicators.note: after means the lock piece comes after the letter A
in a down clue, up means the word is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Lock up the demonstrators after a protest march.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock up' reads like jailing someone, but in a down clue 'up' turns the hair word over, and 'after' puts it behind A.
explanation.definitionFit: To protest one's innocence is to assert or declare it firmly.

clue.text: Look down on French general's conservative objective

parts.note: the Prince de Condé was a celebrated French general; his name with the possessive S
an end is an aim or objective

explanation.surface: A French general's conservative aim is to look down on others.
explanation.definitionFit: To condescend is to behave as if superior, looking down on people.

clue.text: Can change position

explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for jail, like can, and also means to move or budge.

clue.text: Coat to take to the cleaners

definitions.meaning: a sheep's woolly coat, or a warm jacket
slang for to swindle someone out of money

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a woolly coat and also to swindle someone, to take them to the cleaners.

clue.text: Man with a light rug in airport

parts.note: he is a male person
a throw is a light blanket or rug

explanation.surface: A man with a small rug at an airport.
explanation.definitionFit: London's main international airport, an example of an airport.

clue.text: Obscene pictures corporations circulated

indicators.note: circulated means the word is sent round, turned back to front

parts.note: corporation is an old jocular word for a large belly, so tums

explanation.surface: Indecent images were passed round among companies.
explanation.definitionFit: Smut is obscene or indecent material, such as dirty pictures.

clue.text: Army gunners cheat and lie

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners
to diddle is to cheat or swindle

explanation.surface: Soldiers and artillerymen swindle and tell untruths.
explanation.definitionFit: A taradiddle is a petty lie or fib.
